A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Group|group]] and $H$ a [[Definition:Subgroup|subgroup]] of $G$.
Then the [[Definition:Left Coset|left cosets]] of $H$ [[Definition:Set Partition|partition]] $G$, and each has [[Definition:Cardinality|cardinality]] $\order H$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\RR$ be an [[Definition:Equivalence Relation|equivalence relation]] on a set $S$.
Then the [[Definition:Equivalence Class|equivalence classes]] of $\RR$ form a [[Definition:Set Partition|partition]] of $S$.

substitutions.the equivalence relation ~: a ~ b iff a^{-1}b in H

validity_conditions: The relation a ~ b iff a^{-1}b in H is reflexive, symmetric, transitive (using that H is a subgroup).
Its equivalence classes are exactly the left cosets aH.
The general 'equivalence relations partition' theorem then yields the coset partition; equal size follows separately from the bijection h |-> ah.
proof_plan:
Define $a \sim b \iff a^{-1} b \in H$.
$\sim$ is [[Definition:Reflexive Relation|reflexive]] as $e \in H$, [[Definition:Symmetric Relation|symmetric]] as $H$ is closed under [[Definition:Inverse Element|inverses]], and [[Definition:Transitive Relation|transitive]] as $H$ is closed under the group operation.

The [[Definition:Equivalence Class|equivalence class]] of $a$ is:
:$\eqclass a \sim = \set {b: a^{-1} b \in H} = a H$
By [[Relation Partitions Set iff Equivalence]], the equivalence classes partition $G$.
